svg.title: Lab 1 cluster components, step by step
svg.desc: Animated diagram cycling through the seven Lab 1 steps, highlighting the components each step uses or breaks.

g.text: Every arrow points at the API server. The scheduler, controller manager and both worker
kubelets watch it; none of them talk to each other or to etcd directly.
The control-plane kubelet starts the API server, etcd, scheduler and controller manager from
files in /etc/kubernetes/manifests, without asking the API server.
kubectl writes a Deployment. The controller manager creates a ReplicaSet, then Pods. All
three are objects in etcd, linked by ownerReferences.
You delete a pod. The controller manager sees 2 of 3 and creates one, the scheduler assigns
it a node, and that node's kubelet starts it.
kubectl is just an HTTP client. The ?watch=1 stream you open is the same mechanism every
Your stale file carries an old resourceVersion. The API server compares it with etcd and
rejects the write. No locks involved.
With the scheduler gone, the controller manager still creates pods, but nobody assigns them
a node, so they stay Pending.
Deleted pods aren't replaced. When the controller manager restarts it compares desired vs
actual state and catches up, even though it missed the deletes.
